title: The Ferry Bell
summary: The water under King's Parade came from somewhere. Up Bridge Street the Round Church stands in a ring of river-mist, and under Magdalene Bridge an old bell has gone quiet.

intro.line: North of the Market, past Sidney Street, a cold mist is rolling uphill from the river. It does not thin as it climbs. It gathers, in a perfect ring, around the Round Church.

steps.text: Ask Old Mother Gadd for a lift up Bridge Street

dialogue.line: Bridge Street, is it? In this mist? You'll walk into the river before you find the church. Hop in the van, love.
Mind the fryer. And if anything wet tries to get in, hit it.

travel.caption: The chip van rattles north past the Market, up Sidney Street, into the mist.

steps.text: Follow the mist up Bridge Street to the Round Church

dialogue.line: The church is round as a bell-mouth and nine centuries old. Inside it, the little sanctus bell is ringing on its own: one stroke, then a long wet silence, then one more.
Shapes come up Bridge Street out of the mist, dripping. Some carry poles.

steps.text: Drive the drowned back from the Round Church

intro.line: A drowned punter in a rotted blazer, a wraith of Cam water, and an old college bicycle that the moss has stood up on its own wheels.

dialogue.line: The last of them falls apart into weed and river-silt. On the church step lies the sanctus bell's clapper, wrenched out and dropped.

steps.text: Take up the sanctus bell's clapper by the Round Church

dialogue.line: You hang the clapper back on its leather and the sanctus bell rings once, clean and dry. The ring of mist around the church lets go.
Down Bridge Street, iron glints on the setts: the curved stays of a much bigger bell, torn loose and washed uphill.

steps.text: Pick up the first bell-stay on Bridge Street

dialogue.line: Black iron, river-cold, stamped with a little boat. It still smells of the weir.

steps.text: Pick up the second bell-stay nearer the river

dialogue.line: The second stay. From under Magdalene Bridge somebody is whistling, badly, a tune that might once have been a hymn.

steps.text: Find whoever is whistling at the old hythe by Magdalene Bridge

dialogue.line: Evening, guv! Mind the edge, it's slippy. Took me, that edge did. Eighteen ninety-four. Lovely night for it, mind.
You're... wet. Very wet.
Wat Gedney, ferryman, at your service and the river's. Them stays you've got there are off my bell. The Ferry bell. Hung under this bridge since there was a ford here.
Somebody cut it loose a week Tuesday. Since then the drowned don't stay down. Not the friendly sort like me. The other sort.
And the one who's took the bell for his own, he's sat on the bridge. Calls himself the Quant-King. Made of every pole that ever went in the Cam. Clear me a way to him, would you?

steps.text: Clear the drowned from the Quayside

intro.line: The river slops over the Quayside and stands up. A marsh-light bobs above it like a lantern on a pole.

dialogue.line: That's the way! Now look up, guv. On the bridge. That's him.
Something tall unfolds on Magdalene Bridge with a creak of wet wood: a crown of pole-tips, a straw hat the size of a cartwheel, and the Ferry bell hung on its chest like a medal.

steps.text: Defeat the Quant-King of Magdalene Bridge

intro.line: The Quant-King plants its great pole on the bridge and pushes, as if the whole town were a punt it meant to steer into the river.

dialogue.line: The poles come apart one by one and slide into the Cam, lost all over again. The Ferry bell drops, rings once on the bridge, and is still.
You fit the two stays back. Under the arch the bell takes up a slow, low swing, and the river goes quiet and flat.

steps.text: Tell Wat Gedney his bell is hung again

dialogue.line: Hear that? That's the hythe sorted. The drowned'll lie down proper now, the ones as ought.
The Round Church bell, the Ferry bell. Somebody is cutting them loose one at a time.
Somebody with keys and a boat, I'd say. I've seen a lantern going up and down the Backs at night. Not my lantern.
Here: my fare-penny. Kept it in my cheek a hundred and thirty years. You show that to the river and it'll carry you. Quick, like.
When you want the Backs, come and find me. Under the old bell, that's where the drowned go.

travel.caption: Wat poles you back upriver to the Mill Lane steps. You walk up through the sleeping town to Bene't Street.
